title: Token Annotator: adaptive tracing hooks and KV-cache delta attribution
creator: Ava Chen
description: Add a lightweight, adaptive token-level annotator that inserts tracing hooks at emission points and emits metric/log records that capture per-token duration and KV-cache hit/miss deltas. The goal is to provide accurate per-token latency and cost attribution with minimal overhead in high-throughput serving paths. This ticket covers schema design, runtime hook insertion (C++ runtime/Go coordinator), sampling strategy, pipeline enrichment, and dashboard/alert wiring.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits an immutable token-annotator envelope for >=99% of sampled requests containing: token_index, step_duration_ms, prefix_cache_hit(boolean), kv_cache_latency_ms, model_variant, request_id
End-to-end pipeline persists token-level events to the token-events Kafka topic and a transformed message to ClickHouse for aggregation
Grafana dashboard showing per-token p50/p95/p99 latency, kv-cache hit-rate split, and cumulative token cost per request is available in observability/team/redwood-inference/token-annotator
Overhead on P99 tail latency of serving path is <2% when sampling set to 5% and <5% when sampling 25% (validated in load test)
QA tests demonstrate that cache-hit attribution correctly deducts kv cache latency from per-token CPU/GPU time accounting
implementation_notes: Design decisions: (1) Use adaptive sampling: base sample 1% globally, ramp to 25% for requests that show >100ms token emission variance or are in active SLO investigation; sampling tag is set in coordinator. (2) Emit two artifacts: compact binary trace span for internal tracing backend and lightweight JSON event for analytics pipeline. (3) KV cache instrumentation emits pre- and post- timestamps at microsecond resolution; annotator computes delta and flags hit/miss. (4) To avoid payload bloat, only first 64 tokens for long generations are persisted by default; full traces retained for 1% ring buffer. (5) Hook placement: runtime layer (C++) at emit_token(), coordinator (Go) for request-level tags and routing metadata. (6) Privacy: token text is never emitted; only token_index and token_hash are allowed. (7) Backpressure: Kafka producer uses async batching and local disk buffer as fallback during spikes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Instrumentation in staging with default sampling 0.5% - internal validation and perf profiling
Phase 2: Enable analytics pipeline and ClickHouse transforms; run A/B comparing latencies and storage costs
Phase 3: Canary in production for a small customer segment (5% traffic) with detailed dashboards and kill-switch
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 5% global sampling and enable adaptive ramp rules for SLO anomalies
Phase 5: Documentation and SDK examples; enable feature flag for Dedicated/Private customers
testing_plan: Unit tests for annotator logic (hit/miss delta computation, sampling tags)
Integration tests: end-to-end emit -> Kafka -> transform -> ClickHouse
Perf test: 2-hour soak at 2x peak traffic verifying P50/P99 latency overhead bounds
Chaos test: simulate Kafka outages and verify local buffer fallback and no request drop
Security review: confirm no token plaintext or customer PII is included
monitoring_and_dashboard: New Grafana folder observability/team/redwood-inference/token-annotator with panels: token-latency-by-index (p50/p95/p99), kv-cache-hit-rate-by-model, cumulative-cost-per-request, sampling-rate and pipeline lag (Kafka consumer lag). Alerts: token-annotator-consumer-lag>300s, token-p99-regression>15% relative to baseline, kv-cache-hit-rate-drop>10%.
